1. Purpose and scope
This guide gives fictional academic rules for three programmes: B.Tech Computer Science and
Engineering (B.Tech CSE), B.Sc Data Science, and Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA). The
rules are designed so a RAG system can retrieve programme-specific passages.
Student-record boundary: this document contains policy information only. It does not
contain any student's marks, attendance percentage, registered subjects, or examination
result.

3. Credit-load rules
 - A regular semester normally contains 18 to 24 credits.
 - A student may request up to 27 credits after academic-adviser approval if the previous semester
 GPA is at least 8.0 and there is no active backlog.
- A student on academic probation is limited to 18 credits unless the programme office approves a
 recovery plan.
- Audit-only courses appear on the learning record but do not count toward the degree-credit total.

4. Attendance and examination eligibility
The minimum attendance required to write the end-semester examination is 75 percent in each
registered course. Attendance is calculated separately for each course; an overall average does not
replace the course-level requirement.

Assessment pattern
 - Theory course: 40 percent continuous assessment and 60 percent end-semester examination.
 - Laboratory course: 60 percent continuous performance and 40 percent practical examination.
 - A student must obtain at least 40 percent in the end-semester component and at least 50 percent
 overall to pass a course.
Backlog and re-examination
A failed course becomes a backlog. The student should register for the next available
re-examination through the examination portal. A maximum of four active backlogs is allowed before

re-examination through the examination portal. A maximum of four active backlogs is allowed before
the student must meet the programme coordinator to create an academic recovery plan.

5. Course registration and prerequisites
 - Online registration opens ten calendar days before the first teaching day.
 - The add/drop window closes at 5:00 p.m. on the fifth teaching day.
 - A prerequisite course must be passed before registering for the dependent course unless the
 academic committee records a written exception.
- Timetable clashes are not approved. Students should contact their adviser before the add/drop
 deadline.

7. Academic support and escalation
 - For course choice or prerequisite questions: contact the assigned faculty adviser.
 - For attendance correction: first contact the course instructor within five working days of the
 displayed class record.
- For examination registration or hall-ticket problems: contact the Examination Cell.
 - For a programme exception: submit a written request to the programme office; chatbot answers are
 not approvals.
8. Safe answers for the AI assistant

The assistant may explain the rules in this guide and identify the relevant office. It must not claim to
know a student's current attendance, grades, backlog count, registered courses, or eligibility. Those

Demo contact: Academic Help Desk, academic-help@northstar.example. This address is
